original: The game ran out of memory

Raise this instance's maximum allocated memory, and ask less of the heap: lower the render distance, turn off fancy graphics, drop resource packs with large textures. If it still runs out with a lot of headroom, one mod is holding on to memory - take out the most recently added mods first.
The game ran out of class space

Metaspace holds the classes of everything that is loaded, so it fills up with the number of mods rather than the size of the heap. Add -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=512M to this instance's Java arguments, or remove mods.
Raise this instance's maximum allocated memory. If the line above names something other than the heap, it is the mod that asked for the memory, not the amount.
The memory requested cannot be given

The heap this instance asks for is bigger than what this Java can hand over. Lower the maximum memory - the settings page suggests a number for this machine - and check that the Java in use is 64-bit, since a 32-bit one stops being useful somewhere above 1.5 GiB.
Something here was compiled for %1, but this instance is launching with %2. Set a newer Java in this instance's Java settings, or remove the mod that needs it.
A mod needs a newer Java than the one in use
A mod failed while it was starting up

The line above is the mod that actually failed; the class-not-found line after it is the same mod being asked for again. Scroll to the first ExceptionInInitializerError and take out the mod it names, or update it to a build for this version of the game.
A mod is missing something it needs

Install what this line names - usually a library mod that other mods sit on, or a loader new enough for the mods installed. If it is already installed, the version is not the one being asked for: match the number in this line rather than the name.
The same mod is installed twice

Search the mods folder for each name listed and keep one file per mod, the newest. Two files with different names can still hold the same mod, which is what happens when a mod bundles a library that is also installed on its own.
The mods installed do not agree with each other
Fabric writes under this line who wants what version, and often a suggested fix. Follow it: change the version of the named mod, or remove it. Guessing which of the two is at fault wastes an hour.
A mod could not patch the game

A mixin is a mod rewriting the game's own code while it loads, and it fails when the code it expects is not there. The line names the mod the mixin belongs to - replace it with the build for this exact version of the game and of the loader.
The graphics driver cannot open a window

Update the graphics driver from Intel, AMD or Nvidia's own site rather than through Windows Update. On a laptop with two GPUs, force the game onto the one that supports OpenGL; through remote desktop there is no OpenGL at all and the game cannot start.
A native library was not unpacked

The game's own dll and so files are unpacked into a temporary folder when it starts, and an antivirus or a full disk stops that. Let this launcher and its instance folder through the antivirus, then start again.
There is no room left in the texture atlas

Everything the game draws from a texture sheet has to fit in one image. A high resolution resource pack, or a mod adding many custom items, is what overflows it - lower the pack's resolution or remove the mod that adds the most textures.
The game ran out of registration numbers
Versions before 1.13 have a hard limit on how many blocks and items can be registered, and a large pack reaches it. Remove mods or move the pack to 1.13 or newer; there is no setting for this.

The line above names what the game was doing when it stopped. Take out the mod it blames, or ask its author - the whole report is smaller than one screenshot of the log.
